- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 days), model tends to underpredict sharp drops; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >45), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 5 days.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +1.00 after -1.00), model often delays correction; add 1–2 days lag in upward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to capture it; apply 1–3 day lag correction with downward bias.
- If sentiment history includes 3+ consecutive +1.00, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5–10 days.
- If model forecast is >5% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction by 1–3% per day until convergence.
